summary: Six-part biography of Henry Kissinger, the German-born Harvard academic who as Nixon and Ford's national security adviser and secretary of state (1969-1977) prolonged the Vietnam War, secretly bombed Cambodia and Laos, and backed coups and massacres worldwide.

evidence.note: born 1923 in Fürth to a Jewish family; childhood under rising Nazism
family flees Germany for New York in 1938
Harvard studies, thesis and academic career shape his realpolitik
argues for limited tactical nuclear war at the Council on Foreign Relations
Nuclear Weapons and Foreign Policy book on limited nuclear war
Laos special forces and air strikes approved under Nixon and Kissinger
Operation Menu secret bombing of Cambodia
opening of relations with China discussed at length
still alive at release and courted by politicians in recent elections

notes: Setting capped at six codes: DE (childhood), TL, CN, EG/IL/SY, ZW and AO also discussed per footnotes but only first 2,000 words of parts 2-6 seen, so later-part weighting is inferred from descriptions/footnotes. Lifespan end 2023 is from outside knowledge; he was alive at release, so covered_span ends 2022 (release year). Military service in WWII considered for roles but treated as minor.
